dedupe_keys.name: resource recovery and the sherwood plot

description: The authors derive a generalized Sherwood-plot function linking a recovered compound concentration or dilution to recovery costs, with physical arguments involving entropy. They test the relationship econometrically using deterministic and stochastic data from a small industrial unit recovering polyphenols from fruit-juice residual wastewater. The model also considers cost structures and recovery-market formation. This is a documented economic and physical relation with a real treatment-process application. The metadata do not expose a downloadable implementation, the observations, coefficient values or a transferable error bound. The later chemical-leasing contract model is related but has a distinct pricing and payoff purpose. The source describes the stated resource-recovery analysis. The source authors provide this description through Zenodo, whose deposit declares CC BY 4.0 and public document access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain limited to the cases or observations explicitly described. Only metadata and file descriptors were reviewed; no document, measurements, model archive or code was read. Related components retain their source identities and uncertain experimental overlap. Document access and licensing do not establish executable availability or software rights.
